title: toktier parity reading: the added-token literal segmentation column of one family
description: Per-family column of a native-front-end parity reading (CPU arm or GPU arm, named by the reading's schema) for documents that hold added-token literals: chat-shaped variants of the parity documents and the literal-dense battery, compared with the reference oracle. literal_class says whether the face is served by the native literal segmenter (served) or keeps the whole-document reference path (unserved). Each entry of entry_points is one measured entry point of the native router (id_route: the ID route; state_route: the session-state route), with per-document path classes, the bytes each engine encoded, and the guard documents (documents the engine guard sent whole to the reference). The vacuity guard is on bytes: on a served face the reference encodes bytes only inside the listed guard documents (segments.bytes.hf == guard_documents.bytes_hf), the guard-document count is bounded, and in the GPU arm some segment bytes reach the GPU (segments.bytes.gpu > 0, with gpu_share reported); otherwise a silent whole-document fallback would read as zero mismatches. hf_segments_below_crossover counts the documents of a served face on a route whose only backend after the GPU is the reference with every text segment below the GPU crossover: the reference encodes the whole document (code R_INPUT_ADDED_TOKEN, a case of its own, so hf_added_token on a served face stays 0); such documents are listed in below_crossover_documents with their bytes, which count toward segments.bytes.hf beside the guard documents, and they occur only in the GPU arm. hf_span_guard counts the documents of the state route (state_route only, GPU arm only) whose device-produced row the state-route acceptance refused because the text is not stable under the face's normalizer (or the span bridge failed): the reference re-encodes the whole document (code R_INPUT_GUARD_ROUTED), a class of its own, so neither hf_engine_guard nor hf_added_token counts it; such documents are listed in span_guard_documents with their bytes, which count toward segments.bytes.hf beside the guard and below-crossover documents. hf_device_declined (optional key; absent reads 0) counts the documents of a served face, on either entry point, GPU arm only, whose text segment the device itself declined (the execution record shows a fallback R_EXEC_FAULT from the gpu backend with scope segment) and that the reference, the next and only entry of the chain after the device, then encoded whole: a class of its own, so neither hf_engine_guard nor hf_added_token counts it; such documents are listed in device_declined_documents with their bytes, the chain they ran on (exactly gpu then hf) and the event, their bytes count toward segments.bytes.hf beside the other listed documents, and together with the guard documents they are held to the guard bounds (at most 1 % of the documents, rounded down, and 1 % of the bytes). added_frontend_fingerprint names the added-token table the reading was taken on and has to equal the registry record's. Checked by tools/check_reading_forms.py.

covered_literals.description: Divergence-set literals of carried records covered by the battery (informative).

paths.description: Per-document path classes; every document is counted once.

below_crossover_documents.description: Documents counted as hf_segments_below_crossover and the bytes the reference encoded for them (whole documents). Required when that count is above 0.

span_guard_documents.description: Documents counted as hf_span_guard (state route, GPU arm) and the bytes the reference encoded for them (whole documents). Required when that count is above 0.

device_declined_documents.description: Documents counted as hf_device_declined (GPU arm): the device declined a text segment and the reference encoded the whole document. Required when that count is above 0. chain is the fallback chain the entry point ran on; event is the execution-record event that shows the device's decline.
